sentences.text: Dickosteus stands out among ancient armored fish because scientists possess complete body fossils of this creature.
Researchers Miles and Westoll formally named this genus in 1963.
Remains have been unearthed in the regions of Orkney and Caithness within Scotland.
This animal is a member of the class Placodermi, an extinct group of coccosteid arthrodire placoderms within the family Coccosteidae.
These fossils belong to the Middle Devonian period, spanning the Late Eifelian to Early Givetian stages.
Specifically, Dickosteus inhabited waters during the Givetian stage, roughly 387.95 to 382.31 million years ago.
